method: Seven repo zones reviewed in parallel by a workflow; each zone packed its files through the HEARTH gateway to gcp-gemini-pro (Vertex gemini-3.1-pro-preview) for classification, then every PRUNE verdict was re-examined by a skeptic agent that grepped for inbound references and spot-read decision-record-shaped files. 14 agents, 0 errors, ~987k tokens.
premise: Over-pruning was explicitly acceptable: both source repos still exist at C:/work/comfy and C:/work/lumberjacks, and everything here remains in git history.
excluded_from_review: Lumberjacks/src and network/mod were never offered as prune surface. That code builds the five images serving production, so it is proven live.
signals_rejected: Git-history staleness is meaningless in this repo: the subtree merges attribute all 1045 files to the consolidation date. Basename-orphan detection was also discarded for source, since C# is referenced by namespace rather than filename (196 of 199 apparent orphans were live Lumberjacks source).
second_pass_rationale: Per-zone agents left cross-zone incoherence: generated repo-map outputs survived while their generator was pruned, and index READMEs survived pointing only at deleted content. A second pass removed 11 such orphans.

zone_summaries.skeptic_notes:
METHOD: grepped every basename repo-wide from C:\work\baseline excluding .git, plus the two generated indices that produce pure noise (docs/repo-map/, repo-activity.json) and fieldlab/runs/prune-audit/ (this audit's own scratch inventory). Then spot-read the decision-record-shaped files and every reference that landed in live (non-fieldlab) code.

KEY NEGATIVE RESULT -- the deletion set is closed under its own references. Every intra-set call edge stays inside the set: run-experiment.ps1 -> collect-environment.ps1 + validate-run-packet.ps1; run-autonomous-valheim-lab.ps1 -> verify-netcode-probe.ps1 + set-wsl-resource-profile.ps1; run-netcode-probe-cycle.ps1 -> verify-netcode-probe.ps1 + render-dashboard.py; run-omen-smoke.ps1 -> run-loopback-window.ps1 + omen-client-smoke.ps1; bootstrap-wsl-postgres.ps1 -> bootstrap-wsl-postgres.sh; run-valheim-yolo-swarm.ps1 -> run-autonomous-valheim-lab.ps1. No CI exists (.github/workflows/ is absent), no compose file references any of these, and the live roadmap tooling (Lumberjacks/docs/roadmap/valheim-volunteer-roadmap.json) contains ZERO matches for 'fieldlab/scripts/' or 'command-plans/'.

CLAIMS I CHECKED AND CONFIRMED (each was a plausible overturn that did not survive):

1. set-gcp-p7-target.ps1 -- the reviewer's own precondition ('confirm those coordinates are also recorded under infra/gcp/p7/'). CONFIRMED SATISFIED, uphold. The script carries no live IP at all: -PublicIp is a Mandatory param. Everything else it sets is independently recorded in retained infra: SSH target 'comfy-p7' (infra/gcp/p7/README.md:25, PROMOTION-DRILL.md:23), disk /mnt/comfy-p7 (README.md:26, docker-compose.yml, comfy-lumberjacks-p7.service:6), world ComfyEra16 (README.md:27, docker-compose.yml:185 WORLD_NAME), config/world paths (docker-compose.yml:199-200), and the env-file template (environment.example, /etc/comfy-p7/environment). The container name comfy-lumberjacks-p7-valheim-server-1 is just compose-project + the 'valheim-server' service, both in retained files. Its only consumers (run-loopback-window.ps1, omen-client-smoke.ps1, run-omen-smoke.ps1) are all in the deletion set.

2. start-lumberjacks-gateway.ps1 -- the only deletion-set file referenced from LIVE production code: network/mcp/comfy_gateway/toolsurface/valheim.py:1400, inside valheim_lumberjacks_receipts()'s error hint. Uphold anyway: it is a parenthetical in a human-readable string, not an exec path, and the hint already carries the load-bearing fact inline ('Launch with --urls http://0.0.0.0:4000'), as does valheim.py:1596 without naming the script. Production runs the gateway from infra/gcp/p7/docker-compose.yml. ACTION FOR THE DOC/CODE ZONE: valheim.py:1400 becomes a stale path -- drop the '(fieldlab/scripts/start-lumberjacks-gateway.ps1)' clause in the same commit. Note fieldlab/scripts/start-comfy-gateway.ps1 is correctly NOT in the list (it launches the MCP door the Claude session reads through) -- do not let the name similarity sweep it up.

3. run-experiment.ps1 / validate-run-packet.ps1 / analyze-networksense-perf.ps1 -- the strongest overturn candidate, and it fails on inspection. Lumberjacks/docs/network/valheim-volunteer-platform-plan.md IS live (status 'proposed execution plan', parent of the active plan-m1-strict-admission.md, linked from valheim-volunteer-roadmap.json:845 and served by the running Gateway at RoadmapViewEndpoints.cs:32), and its table names run-experiment.ps1 + validate-run-packet.ps1 as 'Basis of automatic session evidence' (line 214) and analyze-networksense-perf.ps1 as 'Post-run client performance report' (line 216). But those are the plan's only three mentions -- they sit in a backward-looking inventory titled 'What is already proved and should be reused', and NO milestone in the plan, in plan-m1-strict-admission.md, or in the roadmap JSON actually schedules invoking them. The live evidence lane is now infra/gcp/p7/scripts/ (New-ReleaseCut.ps1, run-promotion-drill.ps1, validate-release-bundle.ps1, capture-release-manifest.ps1), none of which touch fieldlab/scripts. The packet standard itself is specified in prose in fieldlab/README.md, so the spec survives the runner. Aspirational doc line, not a live consumer -> uphold per default.

4. new-/close-build-request-receipt.ps1 -- fieldlab/BUILD-REQUEST-RECEIPTS.md reads as an active lane and is a receipt/audit workflow, so I read both scripts. Uphold: the doc has exactly one commit ever (56597b9 'Add build request receipt lane') and is linked from nowhere in the repo; the receipts it produces live under fieldlab/runs/build-requests/, which .gitignore:41 excludes, so no committed receipt or ledger.jsonl is orphaned by deleting the writers; and the lane is superseded by HEARTH's create/get/list/update/execute/close_build_request MCP tools. Minor correction to the reviewer's rationale: the scripts do not 'hardcode' C:\work\comfy -- it is an overridable -Repo/-OutDir default. Wrong reason, right verdict. ACTION FOR THE DOC ZONE: fieldlab/BUILD-REQUEST-RECEIPTS.md becomes a runbook for two nonexistent scripts and should be retired alongside them.

5. Command-plans (all 12) -- read two in full (valheim-lumberjacks-shadow-authority.ps1, era16-density-pressure-matrix.ps1). Pure generators: they take -RunDir/-RepoRoot and WRITE summaries, gates, CSVs and operator runbooks into a run folder. They contain no findings or decisions themselves -- the records they produced are under fieldlab/runs/ and fieldlab/evidence/, which are retained. The whole directory goes, and only two handoff docs mention any of them (handoffs/HANDOFF-LUMBERJACKS-PRIORITY-PATH.md:327,379 and handoffs/HANDOFF-CLAUDE.md:23), both as historical narrative.

6. install-dotnet9.ps1 -- 25 lines wrapping Microsoft's own https://dot.net/v1/dotnet-install.ps1 into C:\work\dotnet9. Trivially reconstructible, documents nothing unique. Uphold.

CONSEQUENTIAL DANGLING REFERENCES FOR OTHER ZONES (not reasons to overturn, but they should not be left behind): fieldlab/scenarios/*.yaml declare the deleted scripts as their runners -- valheim-lumberjacks-netcode-probe.yaml:35 'verifier: fieldlab/scripts/verify-netcode-probe.ps1' and :27 run-autonomous-valheim-lab.ps1, valheim-autonomous-lab.yaml:29-30, valheim-era16-volunteer-readiness-baseline.yaml:59 'dry_run_tool: fieldlab/scripts/set-wsl-resource-profile.ps1'. Nothing in it touches the live load-bearing surfaces — no reference to infra/gcp/p7, the five-service release pipeline, the ComfyNetworkSense mod, or the Lumberjacks roadmap system. data/raw/ holds untouched exports of Google Docs/Sheets (SOURCES.md records the live source URLs and retrieval date 2026-07-01, so the inputs are re-fetchable), data/processed/ holds the generated quest catalogs, anomaly reports and a standalone quest-picker.html, and discord-search-export/ is a one-off Chrome content script for scraping Discord search results. Verdict is uniform PRUNE across all 24 files. The two .xlsx trackers were not packed (5.4 MB and 5.9 MB, both over the 256 KiB pack limit and binary), but SOURCES.md identifies them precisely as the guilds' Google Sheets exports feeding this same pruned pipeline — deleting them alone reclaims ~11.3 MB, by far the largest single win in the zone. Classification was done via mcp__hearth__local_generate on backend gcp-gemini-pro in two batches (336 KB and 113 KB packed), both ok:true; the .xlsx pair I judged myself from SOURCES.md.
zone_summaries.skeptic_notes:
Verification method: repo-wide grep excluding .git and the generated docs/repo-map/ blob (index.html embeds a 3.9MB JSON that swamps results), plus a scripted simulation resolving every markdown link in the ENTRYPOINTS list of tests/test_entrypoint_links.py against the proposed deletion set, including directories that would be emptied. Baseline confirmed: `python -m pytest tests/test_entrypoint_links.py tests/test_repo_activity.py -q` = 8 passed. The 5 failures in tests/test_guest_package.py are pre-existing and unrelated (missing fieldlab/runs/releases/m1-clean-20260717-r1.json).

The reviewer's framing premise -- that the harvest pipeline "has no live consumer" / is "dead" -- is contradicted by the repo itself. Root README.md:133 calls recipes/quest-catalogs/ live, recipes/README.md publishes its commands as runnable, and .claude/launch.json ships a launch target for its output. recipes/ was not in this deletion zone, so pruning its declared inputs leaves a live config pointing at missing files.

Two caveats on the upheld list worth passing to the pruner:

1. Upholding the four quest-catalog outputs (2 JSON + 2 anomalies) is only safe BECAUSE the two .xlsx inputs are overturned -- harvest.py can regenerate them. If a later pass deletes the .xlsx after all, those four become unregenerable and should be re-examined. Note the anomaly reports are open questions for the guild to rule on, not settled records.

2. The reviewer's "regenerable" rationale is factually wrong for weapon-choices-joined.json and weapons-economy-balance.json: there is NO committed generator anywhere in the repo (recipes/ contains only quest-catalogs and rank-ladders). Deleting those two plus their two raw CSVs destroys the weapons dataset outright rather than regenerating it. I still uphold all four -- no live consumer and no test breakage, and the brief says over-pruning is acceptable -- but the decision should be made knowing it is one-way, and docs/datasets/weapon-choices.md and docs/datasets/weapons-economy-balance.md will be left describing files that no longer exist.

On discord-search-export: I uphold content.js and manifest.json because nothing references them and the work is finished, but flag an incoherence. The README must survive (link test), and its entire argument is "trust ~150 lines you can read in two minutes -- open manifest.json and content.js and verify there is no network call." Keeping the verification guide while deleting the auditable code inverts its meaning. Cleanest outcomes are all three kept, or all three dropped with root README.md:77 and the HOTSPOTS row edited to remove the link. Do not delete just the code.

If the pruner wants the ~11MB the two .xlsx represent, the honest path is a separate decision to retire recipes/quest-catalogs/ as a whole (inputs, outputs, sources.json, harvest.py, the launch.json target, and the README claims that call it live) -- not a silent input deletion from the data zone.

Also pruned: erasave/ (one-off classification output), quest_select_design/ (self-described historical design snapshot, including its .thumbnail and pasted screenshot), tools/repo_activity.py + its README + test (git-history activity mapper, meaningless after a subtree merge flattened all dates), tools/verify_comfy_lumberjacks_integration.py (verifies the obsolete two-repo split), and tests/test_entrypoint_links.py (link-checks the pruned repo-map docs).
zone_summaries.skeptic_notes:
Systemic issue worth raising before this prune lands. The reviewer's framing -- that community-systems/quest material is 'unrelated to the Valheim server, release pipeline, mod, or roadmap' -- does not match the repo as it currently documents itself. Root README.md says outright "This repo is not one tidy product", and its Session 5 section calls the quest vertical slice "the most interesting build", listing recipes/quest-catalogs/schema.md, quest-view-schema.md, and data/processed/quest-picker.html as entry points. More concretely, the quest chain terminates in shipped mod code: handoffs/comfy-control-surface/Core/Commands/ControlSurfaceCommands.cs:17 loads quest-view.json at runtime. So the quest recipe is not off-purpose at all.

None of docs/, data/, handoffs/, or README.md appear in this zone's deletion list. If the intent really is to remove the whole community-systems subsystem, docs/quest-vertical-slice-architecture.md, data/processed/quest-*, data/README.md's main-flow section, and the README's Session 5 block have to go in the same commit. Pruning only the generators leaves the repo internally inconsistent -- which is also exactly why I overturned tests/test_entrypoint_links.py.

Dangling references the parent must fix even for the deletions I UPHELD:
- tools/repo_activity.py + tools/README.md: root README.md lines 60-83 are a generated block (<!-- repo-activity:end -->) containing the repo-map links, the hotspot table (which links erasave/, framework/, quest_select_design/, recipes/, tools/ READMEs), and the line "Regenerate with `python tools/repo_activity.py --write`". That block must be removed by hand in the same change, since the tool that maintains it is going away. I upheld these on your stated premise that docs/repo-map is pruned in another zone -- if it is not, reverse this one.
- recipes/rank-ladders/example-output.json (upheld): data/raw/SOURCES.md:51 cites it as the era-16 rank transcription baseline for a documented known-drift note. data/raw/ survives, so update that line.
- recipes/rank-ladders/ generally: docs/perspectives/mikers.md:34 has a live markdown link to ../../recipes/rank-ladders/, and docs/kernel.md:136 marks the recipe "done" with that path as evidence.
- framework/AGENTS.md (upheld): docs/tool-proposal.md:85 calls it "the keystone", and docs/method/conversation-extract.md links it four times. Those are historical/proposal prose rather than executable consumers, which is why I let it go -- but the links will break.
- quest_select_design/ (upheld): its own README says "Keep this directory intact when revisiting the interface", and recipes/quest-catalogs/render_quest_picker.py:9 credits the design to "the quest_select_design pass". Both are soft signals; recoverable from C:\work\comfy, so I did not overturn. Note quest_select_design/support.js is a separate copy from network/design_mocks/support.js -- deleting it does not affect the Network Ward mock.

zone_summaries.summary: The root zone holds repo-wide config, orientation docs, and a handful of point-in-time JSON data/config files. KEEP covers the load-bearing plumbing: .gitignore, .mcp.json (live comfy-gateway wiring), LICENSE, README.md (the merged-monorepo orientation doc), and AGENTS.md (drives the live roadmap/journal system). PRUNE covers artifacts tied to finished or offline side-projects: repo-activity.json (activity-script config describing pre-merge eras), steward-config.json (offline Valheim World Viewer, unconnected to the GCP p7 stack or ComfyNetworkSense), waypoints.json (one-off building-cluster data dump from an old world era), and .claude/launch.json (static server for the finished "quest picker" vertical slice). Classification was produced by gcp-gemini-pro over the packed file contents (21.7 KiB, single batch, ok:true); no binaries or oversized files in this zone.
zone_summaries.skeptic_notes: Method: ran a repo-wide grep for each basename excluding .git, then spot-read the four candidate files plus tools/repo_activity.py, tests/test_entrypoint_links.py, the fieldlab command-plan/scenario pair, and the handoffs segment docs. No .github/ CI directory exists in this repo, so no pipeline gate was available to check. steward-config.json upheld because its owning app (ComfyStewardView) is a separate repo at C:\work\ComfyStewardView and every fieldlab reference points at that external path, never at this config; only hits in-repo are self-referential rows in generated docs/repo-map/ artifacts. Mild caveat: its threshold values (sector_size_m, build_risk_zdo_count, hotspot_sigma_multiplier) appear nowhere else in this repo, so a small amount of tuning provenance is lost, but the owning repo retains its own copy. .claude/launch.json upheld because nothing references it (port 8630 appears nowhere else), it only feeds the Claude Code preview tool, and it is 11 lines with a machine-specific hardcoded Python path — trivially recreated; the artifact it served (data/processed/quest-picker.html) stays committed and README-linked.
